item.title: Words across worlds: Moharaj Sharma on language, culture, and belonging in Nepal
item.description: Global Voices interviewed Moharaj Sharma to explore his path as a poet, journalist, and documentarian, and his enduring efforts to elevate Nepali literature, linguistic traditions, and diaspora narratives.

item.title: Australia's under 16 social media ban under microscope at home and abroad
item.description: "The social media feeds that once connected us are now driving us apart. Social media algorithms are flooding young men’s feeds with radical misogynistic content, inciting real-world harm.'

item.title: At COP30, civil society stepped into real, not symbolic, leadership
item.description: After several conferences shaped by restrictions and tensions between governments and social movements, this COP had active voices in the discussions from grassroots organizations, Indigenous peoples, and traditional communities.

item.title: Life at the U.S.–Mexico border under the Trump administration
item.description: The Trump administration has reintroduced some of its most contentious border measures, leading to renewed targeting, detention, and deportation of migrant communities, leaving thousands seeking safety in increasingly perilous conditions.

item.title: Fraudulent networks fuel deforestation and illegal timber exports in Cameroon
item.description: The Cameroonian state incurs a colossal loss amounting to billions of CFA francs each year due to uncollected logging rights, unpaid taxes, and losses related to the underdevelopment of local processing.

item.title: Hong Kong media tycoon Jimmy Lai found guilty under national security law
item.description: Lai was found guilty of conspiring to collude with foreign forces and sedition. The maximum penalty is life imprisonment and the court will determine the final sentence early next year.

item.title: China’s green power in Angola: When clean energy comes with heavy debt
item.description: In recent years, Chinese international investment schemes have increasingly emphasized “green development” and a “Green Belt and Road,” with hydropower positioned as a climate-friendly alternative to fossil fuels.

item.title: Social networks fuel youth mobilization on Argentina’s streets
item.description: Unlike movements in earlier decades, Argentina’s latest youth-led protests are increasingly organized digitally through platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Whatsapp, rather than through unions or political parties.

item.title: China’s green investment in Pakistan: Solar dreams, debt shadows, and the politics of a rapid transition
item.description: China is simultaneously the country enabling Pakistan’s solar boom and the country whose earlier coal investments continue to shape the power system’s financial and environmental burdens.

item.title: Dominican Republic wastes renewable energy while fossil fuel thermoelectric plants operate above legal limits
item.description: Non-compliance with Technical Minimum Power, causing a greater injection of fossil-fuel-generated energy into the grid, violates Dominican legislation and hinders climate commitments, especially when renewable energy companies’ production remains restricted.
